dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Sure thing! In fact, I've got just the story to share.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: As the deacon, I occasionally offer life advice. Recently, a couple approached me separately, each seeking my counsel.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: The husband, a handsome knight and excellent swordsman, was the owner of a treasured family heirloom — an incredibly sharp sword.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, he lacked a suitably valuable sheath, so he usually kept it wrapped in a roll of cloth.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: His wife was a beautiful gardener with a passion for cultivation. Recently, her many years of hard work had finally paid off with the blooming of a rare and stunning flower.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, having no greenhouse of her own, she had to keep the delicate flower at an associate's place.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: As the holidays approached, both husband and wife hoped to surprise each other with the perfect thoughtful gift.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: As you may have guessed, the husband wished to present his wife with a greenhouse of her own. However, being of modest means, his only way to secure the necessary funds was by selling off his sword.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: The wife, on the other hand, wished to give her husband an exquisitely crafted sheath to go with his sword. Like her husband, she could only achieve this by selling away her most prized possession.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Both of them came to ask me if they should make the sacrifice. Which would you have advised to go through with it?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Mm. The quality of a knight's own swordsmanship is indeed far more important than that of their sword. So he should accept the loss and help his wife fulfill her dream.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Still, if his wife ever learned that he had traded in his treasure for her dream, would she really be pleased to accept the gift?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: After all, you can always grow new flowers, even rare ones. But his sword was truly one of a kind.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: In either case, you could argue that trading in their treasure would be a huge mistake. There was no way to do them both justice.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So did you end up turning them both away?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: And ask them to hide their affection? Now, why would I do that? That would only have led to regret. No, this was a rare opportunity to encourage a pair of lovers to break the day-to-day monotony, embrace the festive spirit, and do something truly romantic!

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Isn't it obvious? I encouraged both of them to make the trade-off!

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: I suppose you think I gave them even more cause for regret, huh?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Quite the opposite... If their real goal was to show the other how much they cared, then neither the sword nor the flower truly mattered.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Just imagine the scene when they finally exchanged gifts with each other. I'm sure that made for a festival that neither one of them will ever forget.

choices.text: Wow, what a stroke of genius!

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: #You get me, {NICKNAME}! Neither object was all that important in comparison to a person's love for their partner.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Ah, yes. Even though she would no longer be able to tend to her beloved flower, she could be sure that it would continue to flourish.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: It could still thrive under the care of a fellow master, while her husband's long-time wish would finally be fulfilled.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Still, if her husband ever learned that she had traded in her finest work to grant his wish, would he really be pleased to accept the gift?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: His wife had devoted years of her life to the cultivation of that flower, while the sword was simply something he'd inherited from his father. In other words, he'd done nothing to earn it.
